phase: The menagerie: how animals are generated
slice: The creature generator reviewed and lifted at the root: jointed legs, a frame under the coat, faces with bones, an elder kit for legends, a growth check; then Ed's body profile and spine, so no animal is a sausage
built: `docs/art-review/menagerie-review.md`: the creature pipeline end to end and its weaknesses measured (knee angles, level-to-level silhouette distances)
Legs with real joints and a stance by species: shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw; hip, stifle, hock, paw; hooves, pads and flat soles (`quad3d`)
A frame under the coat: withers, a pelvis, a loin, a brisket, a nape and a throat
Faces with bones: a brow ridge, cheeks, a lower jaw with a mouth line, whiskers
The elder kit: grizzle, a torn ear, a broken tusk or horn, a torc, rings, earrings, leg bands, a garland, bells, for any legend (`evolve3d`)
The growth-not-scale check: each level's silhouette against the level before, scaled to one box

The body profile (`body.profile`): width and depth set apart at five stations along the body (shoulder, ribcage, waist, loin, hip), the torso lofted through them; a wide deep chest and a slim waist for the big cats, the canids and the deer
The spine (`body.spine`): a crest standing on the back line or a groove cut between the back muscles, by station; the boar's bristled crest, the cats' and the wolf's groove, the deer's shoulder line
A view from straight above for the tools (`TOP=1` on the lineup preview), so a body's girth can be judged on a sheet
learned: Measure before you draw: one script through `rigParts` showed nineteen species standing on four vertical columns, which no amount of shading could fix.
A generator change lifts every animal at once, but every knob needs a default that keeps a species itself, or the forty records drift together.
At game scale the smooth union eats small holes: an earring reads as a ring only once its hole is wider than the blend.

Lofting a body through five stations looked right from the side and lumpy from above until the slices ran every tenth of the length with the stations interpolated: the smooth union only hides bumps smaller than its blend.
A groove down the back needs a waist first: cut into a tube it reads as a scratch, cut between two muscle masses it reads as a spine.

previews.caption: Legs with joints and a stance by species: before above, after below (wolf, bear, stag, badger, cheetah, newt)
The elder kit on four legends: a torc and a torn ear, a broken tusk and bronze bands, a bellwether's rings and bells, a shrine fox's earrings
The body profile: the body as built above, with a width/depth profile below, from the side and from straight above (cheetah, lion, tiger, jaguar, wolf; fox, fennec, stag, roe, elk)
The spine: with the profile but no spine above, with a crest or a groove below (boar, lion, tiger, jaguar; cheetah, wolf, stag, elk)
